trigger_and_correction.trigger: Removing an actor image or Canvas-only image previously caused Canvas to clear the whole accelerated prefix before releasing that image. Unrelated surviving geometries/material/textures were unnecessarily disposed and recreated.
trigger_and_correction.ownership: Each GPU texture now acquires its own synchronous ready broker lease and verifies the exact same decoded-image identity. It retains the lease until that texture is incrementally removed, cleared, invalidated/context-retired or disposed.
trigger_and_correction.retirement: GPU texture disposal precedes release of its own decoded-image lease. Canvas can release its separate CPU consumer without closing pixels still owned by the GPU.
trigger_and_correction.compatibility: Canvas skips the old global clear only when it has acquireAsset AND the presenter explicitly advertises ownsImageLeases===true. Borrowed/custom legacy paths retain their prior clear-before-final-CPU-release behavior.
trigger_and_correction.performance_limit: Preserving source/resource identity avoids the demonstrated overclear path. Source/Node counters do not establish actual browser frame timing or eliminate genuinely capacity-driven cold loads.

findings_closed.finding: A first ready GPU image could acquire a texture/lease, then a later asset admission or geometry-construction error left the newly created owner cached without a committed resource.
findings_closed.resolution: Created image entries and borrowed-to-owned lease upgrades are staged and rolled back in reverse on preparation failure. Pending/mismatched leases and texture-construction failure also release their acquisition.

findings_closed.finding: A resource written successfully before a later resource failed could retain sources/groups/instance data pointing to a disposed rolled-back texture.
findings_closed.resolution: Failure-only successfully touched resources are removed from every cache key and referencing instance; each geometry is freed once and its sources/groups cleared before image rollback. Untouched committed resources remain reusable. Resource fast paths additionally verify the imageMap owns the actual source texture, including borrowed legacy retry.
